教.meaning: Out of <part>filial piety</part>, a boy lets his old grandpa lean on his shoulder. In return, grandpa points his folding <part>fan</part> at the blackboard: letters, sums, the names of the stars. The old man loves to <kanji>teach</kanji>.
教.on: Today grandpa's fan taps a postcard of <sound>Kyo</sound>to, and the class must chant the city's name, holding its first part long and slow until he nods.
教.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' says the boy, finally getting it, and draws a <sound>shee</sound>p on the board.

転.meaning: A <part>kite</part> string gets tangled round the wheel of a <part>car</part>. The car spins round and round, the kite loops in circles above it, and the driver gets dizzy. Everything starts to <kanji>revolve</kanji>.
転.on: A <sound>ten</sound>or on the roof spins with it, singing one long note the whole time.
転.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala and a <sound>ro</sound>dent cling to the bumper as the car rolls off downhill.

送.meaning: An <part>alien</part> stands at the foot of a <part>ramp</part> with a parcel under each arm, pushes them up into its little spaceship and waves them off to its mum on Mars. Every week it has something to <kanji>send</kanji>.
送.on: This week's parcel is a giant bar of <sound>soa</sound>p, because Mars is very dusty.
送.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' says its mum, opening the box, and out pops a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo.

住.meaning: A <part>lord</part> hangs his cloak on the <part>coat hook</part> by the door, kicks off his boots and puts his feet up. This isn't a visit: his name is on the mailbox. This is the house where he will <kanji>dwell</kanji>.
住.on: He keeps his best <sound>jew</sound>el on the mantelpiece, so everyone knows this is his home.
住.kun: Every night he eats <sound>su</sound>shi in his slippers by the fire.

亡.meaning: An old sailor lies down in a long wooden <part>drawer</part> for his final rest, and his friends set a <part>lid</part> with a little knob on top. They hum his favourite song and say goodbye to the <kanji>deceased</kanji>.
亡.on: They roll a <sound>bou</sound>lder up beside the grave to mark the spot.
亡.kun: On the boulder they leave his last <sound>na</sound>an, for the journey.

忘.meaning: A <part>tombstone</part> sits right on top of your <part>heart</part>, pressing down on everything you once knew: your keys, your homework, your best friend's birthday. All of it buried. You <kanji>forget</kanji>.
忘.on: A <sound>bou</sound>lder sits in your path, and you walk straight into it: you forgot it was there.
忘.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' you cry, halfway through lunch: you forgot the soy sauce for your <sound>su</sound>shi.
